question: Should Discord Activity support continue from this older branch, move to the newer broader Discord Activities PR, or restart as a Canvas-plugin-owned design with fail-closed Activity auth?
rationale: The unresolved choice crosses plugin ownership, Gateway authorization, credential transport, operator config shape, and overlapping open PRs, so automation can identify blockers but should not choose the permanent Activity security boundary.

options.title: Rebuild under Canvas plugin auth
options.body: Port the work to `extensions/canvas` and `extensions/discord`, require explicit Activity credentials, avoid URL tokens, bound fanout, and add live Discord proof before merge.

options.title: Continue through the newer PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/65205 as the working branch only after resolving its similar security, compatibility, proof, and merge-state blockers.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Leave Discord Activities out of core until maintainers settle the security model and whether this belongs in the Canvas plugin or an external package.

recommendation.title: Rebuild under Canvas plugin auth
recommendation.body: Port the work to `extensions/canvas` and `extensions/discord`, require explicit Activity credentials, avoid URL tokens, bound fanout, and add live Discord proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The blocker is primarily a Canvas plugin and Gateway auth boundary decision, and recent history points most strongly to this handle for that seam.
